title: Categorical constancy of complete Segal spaces and rowwise weak equivalences
statement:
Use the simplicial spaces, vertical Reedy fibrancy, complete Segal spaces and Rezk weak equivalences of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model], and categorical equivalences of simplicial sets in the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. For a bisimplicial set $X$ call $X_{\bullet,q}$ its row of vertical degree $q$. If $X$ is a vertically Reedy fibrant complete Segal space, then every row $X_{\bullet,q}$ is a quasicategory and, for each $q\geq0$, the map
$$X_{\bullet,0}\longrightarrow X_{\bullet,q}$$
induced contravariantly by the unique map $[q]\to[0]$ in the vertical simplex variable is a categorical equivalence. For any map $f:X\to Y$ of bisimplicial sets, if $f_{\bullet,q}$ is a categorical equivalence for every $q\geq0$, then $f$ is a Rezk weak equivalence. The last assertion does not require $X$ or $Y$ to be fibrant.

source.place: Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 4.5; row quasicategories from Proposition 3.4. This is the horizontal regularity and weak-equivalence comparison, before the first-row Quillen equivalence of Theorem 4.11. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Use the division notation and vertical model of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. Choose the vertex inclusion $v:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^q$ at $0$ and the collapse $t:\Delta^q\to\Delta^0$. The inclusion $v$ is a Kan trivial cofibration: it is monic, and on geometric realizations the homotopy $(x,s)\mapsto(1-s)x+se_0$ contracts the standard geometric simplex to that vertex. Vertical Reedy fibrancy therefore makes $d=X/v:X/\Delta^q\to X/\Delta^0$ lift all monomorphisms. Since Joyal cofibrations are precisely monomorphisms, the Joyal weak factorization system makes $d$ a Joyal trivial fibration. The canonical degeneracy map is $s=X/t:X/\Delta^0\to X/\Delta^q$, and contravariance and $tv=1$ give $ds=1$. Two-out-of-three implies that $s$ is a categorical equivalence. Under representable evaluation $X/\Delta^q=X_{\bullet,q}$; this proves categorical constancy, including $q=0$, where $s=1$. This argument needs vertical Reedy fibrancy alone.

source.place: Propositions 2.5 and 2.8; forward direction of Proposition 4.4

proof.text: Let $W$ be a vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space (in particular $X$, and every Rezk-fibrant object of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model]). For a simplicial set $T$ the division $W/T$ of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus] has $(W/T)_p=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(\Delta^p\boxtimes T,W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(T,W_p)$, with the same operators, so it is the simplicial set $W/T$ of [lem-coef-segal-vertical-restriction-inner]; vertical Reedy fibrancy is Reedy fibrancy for the Kan model structure. That node makes $W/T$ a quasicategory for every $T$ and $W/b:W/T\to W/S$ an inner fibration for every monomorphism $b:S\hookrightarrow T$. Taking $W=X$ and $T=\Delta^q$, the row $X_{\bullet,q}=X/\Delta^q$ is a quasicategory. No completeness is needed for this step.

source.place: Proposition 3.4, (i) implies (v), with v the monomorphism from the empty simplicial set; rows are the representable divisions (Section 2)

proof.text: Let $p:U\to V$ be a Rezk fibration between complete Segal spaces. First $p$ is a vertical Reedy fibration. Indeed let $j$ be a vertical trivial cofibration and let $Z$ be any complete Segal space. The vertical simplicial model axiom makes $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(j,Z)$ a trivial Kan fibration because $Z$ is vertically Reedy fibrant. The mapping-space definition of Rezk weak equivalences therefore makes $j$ a Rezk weak equivalence. Both model structures have monomorphisms as cofibrations, so every vertical trivial cofibration is a Rezk trivial cofibration. The map $p$ lifts them all, and hence is a vertical fibration by the vertical weak factorization system. This uses only the Rezk mapping tests and existence, not the mixed Joyal/Kan box-product assertion of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model].

source.place: Theorems 2.6 and 4.1: vertical-to-Rezk trivial-cofibration inclusion; preliminary to Lemma 4.3

proof.text: For an inner horn $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ form $r_a=\langle a\backslash p\rangle:B\backslash U\to P_a=(B\backslash V)\times_{A\backslash V}(A\backslash U)$. It is a Kan fibration by step 3 and the vertical division criterion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. The absolute restriction $a\backslash U:B\backslash U\to A\backslash U$ is the map $\langle a\backslash(U\to *)\rangle$, since $B\backslash *$ is terminal. By the division lifting bijection, $\delta_m\pitchfork(a\backslash U)$ is equivalent to $a\pitchfork(U/\delta_m)$, and $U/\delta_m$ is an inner fibration by step 2; so $a\backslash U$ lifts every boundary inclusion $\delta_m$, $m\geq0$, and is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The same holds for $a\backslash V$. The projection $P_a\to A\backslash U$ is a pullback of $a\backslash V$ and still lifts all boundary inclusions. Its composite with $r_a$ is $a\backslash U$; two-out-of-three makes $r_a$ a weak homotopy equivalence and hence a trivial Kan fibration, which lifts every monomorphism. For every monomorphism $b:S\hookrightarrow T$, transposing its lifting against $r_a$ by the division bijection shows that $\langle p/b\rangle:U/T\to(V/T)\times_{V/S}(U/S)$ lifts every inner horn. Its domain $U/T$ is a quasicategory by step 2. Its target is also one: $V/b:V/T\to V/S$ is an inner fibration by step 2, so its pullback to $U/S$ is an inner fibration, and the base $U/S$ is a quasicategory by step 2; a horn lifts first to the base and then through this inner fibration. Thus $\langle p/b\rangle$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories.

source.place: Proposition 3.10, proof using Proposition 3.4 and division adjunction (2.1)

proof.text: Let $J$ be the full nerve of the walking isomorphism and $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ its endpoint inclusion, as in [lem-coef-complete-segal-walking-isomorphism]. Completeness makes both $u_0\backslash U:J\backslash U\to U_0$ and $u_0\backslash V:J\backslash V\to V_0$ trivial Kan fibrations. The relative restriction $r_0:J\backslash U\to(J\backslash V)\times_{V_0}U_0$ is a Kan fibration by step 3. Projection of its target to $U_0$ is the pullback of $u_0\backslash V$, hence a trivial Kan fibration; its composite with $r_0$ is $u_0\backslash U$. Two-out-of-three makes $r_0$ a trivial Kan fibration. It lifts every monomorphism $b:S\hookrightarrow T$. Transposing this lift gives $u_0\pitchfork\langle p/b\rangle$. Step 4 and [lem-coef-joyal-walking-isomorphism-fibration-test] therefore make $\langle p/b\rangle$ a Joyal fibration. In particular this holds for $b=\delta_q$ in all degrees, including $\delta_0:\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$, so $p$ is a horizontal Reedy fibration.

source.place: Lemma 4.3; Lemma 4.2 and Proposition 1.13; forward direction of Proposition 4.4

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-quillen-fibrant-test] to the identity adjunction $L=\mathrm{id}$ from the horizontal model structure of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus] to the Rezk model structure of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model], with right adjoint $R=\mathrm{id}$. Both model structures have the monomorphisms as cofibrations, so by their weak factorization systems both have as trivial fibrations exactly the maps with the right lifting property against all monomorphisms; hence $R$ sends Rezk trivial fibrations to horizontal trivial fibrations. By step 5, $R$ sends every Rezk fibration between Rezk-fibrant objects (the vertically Reedy fibrant complete Segal spaces) to a horizontal fibration. The cited criterion makes the identity a Quillen adjunction: the identity from the horizontal structure preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.5, first statement, via Proposition 7.15 (with Lemma 7.14)

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ now be any rowwise categorical equivalence. It is a weak equivalence in the horizontal Reedy model structure, whose objects are all cofibrant. The weak-equivalence preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], applied to the identity adjunction of step 6, therefore makes $f$ a Rezk weak equivalence. Its domain and codomain need not be fibrant in either structure. This proves the last assertion without applying a fibrant-object theorem to arbitrary bisimplicial sets.

Wrote the relative inner-horn and walking-isomorphism lifting arguments, then the identity Quillen argument and its all-cofibrant consequence. Added three statement-only technical dependencies after DAG, blueprint, Lean and logged Mathlib searches. Corrected doubled TeX escapes without changing the proposition. Avoided Proposition 4.6 because its source proof uses Theorem 4.5. Maintainer review: the inner-horn restriction is taken from the existing lem-coef-segal-vertical-restriction-inner (Joyal-Tierney 3.4 (v)) by the division transposition, and the identity Quillen criterion from the existing lem-coef-quillen-fibrant-test (Proposition 7.15 form); the two duplicate new nodes were dropped.
